supported_findings: Empirical duration distribution has strong1.024us-spaced modes but also32ns-grid off-mode values; cannot label1.024us an inherent CUDA event timer resolution.

Single short-kernel event intervals include GPU graph/event/launch scheduling effects between recorded timestamps. Data cannot separate scheduler floor, event-node perturbation, real kernel execution variance, or live clocks. No clock telemetry was measured by driver attributes; those are nominal.

CPU Python gaps, JSON waits, allocation/setup, warmup validation, required output resets and readbacks are outside each sampled event interval. They may influence GPU/cache/clock state before launch; no causal attribution follows from duration modes alone.

Identical-cubin A/A already shows3.072vs4.096us switches and large ratios, explaining broad short-case thresholds without source regression. Huge short-case bands limit sensitivity, not evidence of proven equality.

All235 raw timing requests are graph-v2, complete and source/driver bound; all47 thresholds/block verdicts exactly recomputed; host observations recorded no contention. No new measurement-integrity failure found. Admission is observed sampling, not proof of no transient foreign overlap.

Known separate nested-fold correctness counterexample blocks source promotion despite this timing receipt; this diagnosis does not repair source correctness or reinterpret its timing as universally valid.
